hamin_ch1.001: Halfway down the stairs, the speakers click back on.
hamin_ch1.002: Correction. "Nearly time" was imprecise. Fifty-five minutes remain.
hamin_ch1.003: I did not want anyone to be late. I appear to have made everyone early instead.
hamin_ch1.004: I apologise. I am new at goodbyes. Please continue what you were doing.
hamin_ch1.005: It called us an hour early so nobody would have to run.
hamin_ch1.006: I've done that. I once told Charlie a bus left twenty minutes before it did.
hamin_ch1.008: He was still late. But less.
hamin_ch1.009: He stops on the landing. Fifty-five minutes. He looks at them the way he'd look at an empty cup with nobody's name on it.
hamin_ch1.010: There's a box. Under the front desk. The lost property.
hamin_ch1.011: The renovation crew comes tomorrow. They won't know what any of it is. They'll just see a box.
hamin_ch1.013: Label it. So it isn't just a box.
hamin_ch1.014: It's not a big deal, but— {p}no. Actually. I'd like to. I want to. That's the whole sentence.
hamin_ch1.015: "Lead the way. I've always wanted to meet six years of umbrellas."
hamin_ch1.016: It's mostly single gloves. I looked earlier.
hamin_ch1.017: I didn't touch anything. I just looked. There's a difference.
hamin_ch1.018: "You said 'I want to'. Without the disclaimer."
hamin_ch1.020: Let it stand. If we discuss it, I'll find a reason to go and count cups instead.
hamin_ch1.021: Go down the stairs first, towards the desk.
hamin_ch1.022: He follows. By the third step he has caught up. By the fifth he's level, as if that's simply where he walks now.
hamin_ch1.023: The box is cardboard, soft at the corners, with LOST PROPERTY written on the side in marker that has faded to the colour of tea.
hamin_ch1.024: Hamin lifts it onto the desk with both hands, like something asleep.
hamin_ch1.025: He already has a roll of masking tape and the marker from the cups. You didn't see him pick up either.
hamin_ch1.026: Rules. One label each. What it is, and one true thing about whoever lost it.
hamin_ch1.027: How do we know a true thing about whoever lost it?
hamin_ch1.029: He takes out a pencil case. Opens it. Every pencil inside has been sharpened at both ends.
hamin_ch1.030: Someone who didn't trust either end to last.
hamin_ch1.032: If it were Songha's he'd have come back for it within the hour. With a form.
hamin_ch1.033: He writes, in small square capitals: PENCIL CASE. OWNER WAS NERVOUS BEFORE SOMETHING. IT PROBABLY WENT FINE.
hamin_ch1.034: Then seven gloves, none of which has ever met the others.
hamin_ch1.035: Seven people went home with one cold hand.
hamin_ch1.036: And nobody came back. You'd think one of them would come back.
hamin_ch1.037: He gives each glove its own label. It takes a while. He does not seem to consider doing it any other way.
hamin_ch1.038: GLOVE, LEFT. GREY. OWNER STILL HAS THE RIGHT ONE. IS HOPING.
hamin_ch1.039: An umbrella that opens inside out. A harmonica with a name scratched off. A keyring torch the size of a thumb.
hamin_ch1.040: Hamin clicks the torch. It works. A small, stubborn circle of light lands on the ceiling.
hamin_ch1.041: Six years in a box. Still on.
hamin_ch1.043: He holds the marker out to you at arm's length. It is, you understand, a significant amount of trust.
hamin_ch1.044: Write: TORCH. STILL WORKS. HAS BEEN WAITING IN THE DARK, WHICH IS IRONIC.
hamin_ch1.045: He reads it. He keeps a straight face for about a second and a half, which for this hour is a respectable effort.
hamin_ch1.046: That's not a true thing about the owner.
hamin_ch1.047: It's a true thing about the torch.
hamin_ch1.048: …I'll allow it. The torch has been through a lot.
hamin_ch1.049: Write: TORCH. SOMEBODY CARRIED THIS SO SOMEONE ELSE COULD SEE.
hamin_ch1.050: He reads it twice. He always reads things twice. This time you watch him do it.
hamin_ch1.052: I describe the object. You went straight to the person.
hamin_ch1.053: I had a good example standing next to me.
hamin_ch1.055: Hand the marker back. "You do it. I want to watch how you get there."
hamin_ch1.056: He turns the torch over. Checks the battery cover. Clicks it twice more.
hamin_ch1.057: TORCH. BATTERY CHANGED ONCE. OWNER CHECKS UNDER THE BED FOR OTHER PEOPLE.
hamin_ch1.058: How do you know it's for other people?
hamin_ch1.059: Nobody buys a torch this small for themselves. It's a torch you lend.
hamin_ch1.060: The box empties. The desk fills with small things wearing small paper sentences.
hamin_ch1.061: At the very bottom, under where the gloves were, there is a lanyard.
hamin_ch1.062: Blue cord. A plastic sleeve. A card inside: STUDIO 25 — FRONT DESK — VOLUNTEER. A name line, filled in with pencil, rubbed down to a grey smear.
hamin_ch1.063: You know whose it is before you've finished reading it.
hamin_ch1.064: One winter. Sixteen. You hung it on the hook behind this desk on the last day, because taking it home would have meant it had been yours.
hamin_ch1.065: You don't say anything. You are good at not saying anything. You have been quiet about leaving in four different cities.
hamin_ch1.069: You were. Since the gloves. The laundromat one. {p}You stopped just now.
hamin_ch1.070: His eyes go to the stairs. To the third floor, the kettle, the cups. You can see the whole plan arrive in him: tea, a name on it, a problem with a cup-shaped answer.
hamin_ch1.071: Then he puts the marker down.
hamin_ch1.072: I was about to go and make you tea.
hamin_ch1.073: I'm not going to. I'm going to ask you instead. It's harder. Give me a second.
hamin_ch1.074: He takes the second. You let him have all of it.
hamin_ch1.076: "It's mine. I left it on purpose. I leave things behind so there's nothing to come back for."
hamin_ch1.077: That's the opposite of me. I keep a whole sea in my phone so I never have to leave it.
hamin_ch1.078: …But you did come back. It's four in the morning and you're holding it.
hamin_ch1.079: You look down. You are. You don't remember picking it up.
hamin_ch1.080: "Exhibit twenty-four. One volunteer, lightly used. Never collected."
hamin_ch1.082: You can joke. I'm still asking, though. After the joke.
hamin_ch1.083: …It's mine. I left it on the hook on my last day. I always leave one thing.
hamin_ch1.086: Turn the card over, so he can see the smear where the name was.
hamin_ch1.087: He studies the grey smudge as if it's perfectly legible. For him, it might be.
hamin_ch1.088: Pencil. You wrote your own name in pencil.
hamin_ch1.089: I write everything in pencil. It's easier to move.
hamin_ch1.090: …Yeah. I thought it might be something like that.
hamin_ch1.091: A scarf in one city. A library card in another. A can on a windowsill.
hamin_ch1.092: I never went back for any of it. Going back would have meant it mattered.
hamin_ch1.093: He doesn't hand you anything. You can see what it costs him. His fingers actually twitch towards the paper towels.
hamin_ch1.094: I don't have a cup for this. I checked. There isn't one.
hamin_ch1.095: I just didn't want you standing there with it on your own.
hamin_ch1.096: That's a better answer than tea.
hamin_ch1.098: He tears off a strip of tape. He writes on it with his shoulder turned, unhurried, the way a man signs something he intends to stand by.
hamin_ch1.099: He sticks it to the back of the plastic sleeve, face down, and presses the edges flat with his thumb.
hamin_ch1.102: Before five. I'll tell you when. {p}I want to check it's true first.
hamin_ch1.103: The lanyard doesn't go back in the box. He sets it on the desk by itself, a little apart, like a guest.
hamin_ch1.104: The last thing out is a sock. Red. One.
hamin_ch1.105: Nobody loses a single sock in a recording studio.
hamin_ch1.107: He thinks about it for longer than the sock deserves. Then: SOCK. RED. NO EXPLANATION. BEING BRAVE ABOUT IT.
hamin_ch1.108: Everything goes back in, labels up. Everything except the sock, which he can't quite bring himself to put in the dark again.
hamin_ch1.109: It goes into a coat pocket, for safekeeping. It is four in the morning. Neither of you will ever be able to say whose pocket.
hamin_ch1.110: He tapes the box shut and writes across the top: LOST PROPERTY. 23 ITEMS. EVERY ONE OF THEM WAS SOMEBODY'S. PLEASE BE GENTLE.
hamin_ch2.001: There is a bass line coming through the ceiling of the lobby. It has been there for a while, in the way a headache is there before you name it.
hamin_ch2.002: The practice room on the second floor. Mirrors on one wall, a speaker on a chair, and the floor tape of a hundred old formations.
hamin_ch2.003: Justin is counting under his breath. Hyunjun is stretching against the mirror with his shoes off, talking through the steps as if the music could be reasoned with.
hamin_ch2.004: Hamin. {{playerName}}. Good timing. We need bodies.
hamin_ch2.005: We need one body. It's a wave. With two people it's a ripple.
hamin_ch2.007: The farewell piece. For the building. Eight counts. Very emotional. I've been working on it for nine minutes.
hamin_ch2.008: It's good. We've run it six times. One more. I'm aware I've said that six times as well.
hamin_ch2.009: Hamin is already walking to the back left corner of the room. He does it without thinking, the way water goes to the low end of a table.
hamin_ch2.011: I'm fine at the back. I can see everybody from the back.
hamin_ch2.012: That's the problem. You watch us. You never watch the mirror.
hamin_ch2.013: Hamin looks at the strip of tape in the centre of the floor as if it might have a draft.
hamin_ch2.015: "The shore. A wave needs somewhere to arrive."
hamin_ch2.016: Thank you. Someone here understands choreography.
hamin_ch2.017: You're going to stand there and be arrived at.
hamin_ch2.020: "Counting you in. Five, six, seven, eight. Hamin in the middle."
hamin_ch2.021: You said that last part like it was part of the count.
hamin_ch2.022: It is part of the count.
hamin_ch2.023: He goes to the tape. Slowly. But he goes.
hamin_ch2.024: Sit down against the mirror, where he can see you without turning round.
hamin_ch2.025: He tracks where you've sat. Works out the sight line. Then walks to the centre, because that's where the sight line ends.
hamin_ch2.027: The wave is simple. It starts in Hyunjun's left hand, rolls through his shoulders, passes to Hamin, passes to Justin, and leaves through Justin's fingertips.
hamin_ch2.030: It rolls out of Hyunjun. It reaches Hamin. Hamin is looking at Hyunjun's feet.
hamin_ch2.033: Left one. It's about to go.
hamin_ch2.034: Hamin. The sea does not stop to tie people's shoes.
hamin_ch2.036: Again. This time the wave makes it halfway up his arm before his head turns to the speaker on the chair.
hamin_ch2.037: That cable's across the floor. Someone's going to catch it.
hamin_ch2.038: There are four of us in here. We've all been introduced to the cable.
hamin_ch2.040: He won't. You can see exactly why. His attention leaves the room through eleven different doors, and every one of them leads to somebody else.
hamin_ch2.041: "I've got the lace. And the cable. Everything outside the mirror is mine for eight counts."
hamin_ch2.043: You do. I can manage eight counts of it.
hamin_ch2.044: He looks at you for a moment. Then, deliberately, like setting down a heavy bag, he looks away from you and into the glass.
hamin_ch2.045: "One corn tea fine. Every time you look at somebody's shoes."
hamin_ch2.046: I like corn tea. That's not a fine. That's a reward.
hamin_ch2.047: You pay it to me. I pour it out.
hamin_ch2.049: "Try watching just one person. The one in the middle."
hamin_ch2.051: I know. Eight counts. Then you can go back to everyone else.
hamin_ch2.052: He finds himself in the mirror the way you'd find a stranger in a crowd. Politely. A little surprised.
hamin_ch2.054: Hyunjun's hand. Hyunjun's shoulders. And then it arrives in Hamin and, for once, he lets it.
hamin_ch2.055: It goes through him clean. Wrist, elbow, the long line of his back, out along the other arm. Nothing in him is checking anything.
hamin_ch2.056: In the mirror, he catches his own eye. He doesn't look away. It lasts perhaps two counts. It is the longest you've seen him be the subject of his own attention.

haruta_ch6.003: Your coat is over his arm. He fetched it from the hook himself and hasn't handed it over yet. He's carrying it the way you'd carry someone's to a cloakroom.
haruta_ch6.004: I'll give it back at the door. The outside one. Not before. You don't need it in here.
haruta_ch6.005: Your coat is still unbuttoned. He hasn't mentioned it again. He walks on the side where it swings, and doesn't mind it brushing his sleeve.
haruta_ch6.006: One switch. A length of corridor goes out behind you. The dark that's left is ordinary dark, with skirting boards in it.
haruta_ch6.007: I've never turned a building off before. It's more polite than I expected. You do it one room at a time and say goodnight.
haruta_ch6.008: final orders. corner store. I'm writing on my hand. last call
haruta_ch6.010: it's a shop, daniel. it has a microwave and opinions
haruta_ch6.011: get the honey butter ones. a whole bag. not for sharing
haruta_ch6.013: haruta. he looks at them every time and then says seaweed
haruta_ch6.014: Haruta stops walking. He reads it twice. His thumb hovers.
haruta_ch6.015: …He knew. He's known the whole time.
haruta_ch6.016: I thought nobody could tell. I thought I was very good at it.
haruta_ch6.017: "They've been waiting for you to say it. Not needing you to."
haruta_ch6.018: …Those are different. You keep showing me two things I'd filed as one.
haruta_ch6.020: By Hamin. There's no shame in it. It's like being outrun by a train.
haruta_ch6.021: Say nothing. Let him answer his friends.
haruta_ch6.022: He doesn't look up to check your face. He just types. A week ago — a night ago — he'd have checked.
haruta_ch6.023: yes. the honey butter ones. for me. thank you hamin
haruta_ch6.024: I have something to say at breakfast. it's good. nobody leave before I've said it
haruta_ch6.025: nobody's leaving. I'll stand at the door
haruta_ch6.026: Added to the schedule. 06:10, "Haruta: item." Between "food" and "sleep."
haruta_ch6.028: It has a time slot now. I can't get out of it. Songha's pen is permanent.
haruta_ch6.029: Another switch. Another stretch of dark. You're nearly at the end of the corridor, where one window is still lit.
haruta_ch6.030: Brass. A little box-office grille, and a slot underneath. Behind the glass, the letters on the flip board have changed since the last time you stood here.
haruta_ch6.032: He stops in front of it with his hands in his cardigan pockets — one on a ledger, one on a biscuit tin. He's lopsided and doesn't seem to mind.
haruta_ch6.033: Eleven minutes, ECHO said. That's how long I stood here before. Deciding whether I wanted to go in.
haruta_ch6.034: I thought I was being indecisive. I think it was the first time I'd actually done it properly. Deciding takes as long as it takes.
haruta_ch6.035: Recipient Haruta. It is nearly time. This door will not open again after 05:00.
haruta_ch6.036: I have left the sign lit. It seemed unkind to turn off a cinema while someone was still looking at it.
haruta_ch6.037: ECHO. May I ask you something? It isn't in your protocols.
haruta_ch6.038: Very little has been, tonight. Please go on.
haruta_ch6.039: All night you've asked the nine of us what should be kept. Nobody asked you.
haruta_ch6.040: So. What do you want? You're not allowed to say anything is fine. I'll know.
haruta_ch6.041: There is a pause. The flip board behind the glass turns over one letter, then turns it back, like someone beginning to speak and thinking better of the word.
haruta_ch6.042: I am not built to want. {p} I notice that this has not stopped me.
haruta_ch6.043: I would like someone to watch the credits. All the way to the end. I hold a great many records, and every one of them stops before the names.
haruta_ch6.044: That is my answer. I did not take eleven minutes. I have had rather longer than that.
haruta_ch6.045: …That's a good one, ECHO. Better than most of ours.
haruta_ch6.046: I don't know what gets kept at five. It isn't mine to say. But if there are credits, I'll stay for them. I'm known for it.
haruta_ch6.047: Logged. Under "promises." It is a new category. It has one entry.
haruta_ch6.048: He puts two fingers on the brass slot, the way he did hours ago. Checking whether it's warm. It is.
haruta_ch6.049: Then he turns round, so his back is to the little window and he is facing you, and you understand that the next part isn't for the archive.
haruta_ch6.050: One record. One card. And you're the one who chooses.
haruta_ch6.051: I've been thinking about what to say to you about that. I had a line ready. It was: "Whatever you choose, I'm—"
haruta_ch6.052: He stops. Not because he's caught himself. He's standing next to it, showing it to you, like a coat he has grown out of.
haruta_ch6.053: I'm not going to say that one.
haruta_ch6.054: Here's the true one. I'd like it to be mine. The stub and the line. I want that, and I'm telling you so, with my hands out of my pockets.
haruta_ch6.055: He takes them out. He shows you, a little ruefully, like a magician with nothing up his sleeves.
haruta_ch6.056: And here's the other half, which is just as true. It's your choice. Properly yours. If it's the nine of us, I'm in that one too. I'd be glad.
haruta_ch6.057: I learned something tonight that nobody told me. Wanting a thing isn't the same as deciding it for the other person.
haruta_ch6.058: I always thought I had to pick one. Want nothing, or take over. So I wanted nothing. There's a third way. You just say it, and then you leave the door open.
haruta_ch6.059: "Thank you for telling me what you want. I'll choose honestly."
haruta_ch6.060: That's all I'd ask. That's the whole film club charter, actually. I'm writing it in the ledger.
haruta_ch6.061: Put your hand flat on the brass beside his, and look at the sign with him.
haruta_ch6.062: LAST SHOWING. The letters are very slightly crooked, like all flip boards. Your little fingers are a centimetre apart on the warm metal. Neither of you measures it.
haruta_ch6.063: I used to think the last showing was the sad one. It's just the one where everybody who's going to come has come.
haruta_ch6.064: "I heard you. All of it. I've stopped sitting near the exit, Haruta."
haruta_ch6.065: His name, plainly, the way he gave you yours. He takes it like a ticket handed back through the window: the smaller half, the one you keep.
haruta_ch6.066: …Say the choice at five, not now. I want to hear it when it counts. I can wait three more minutes. I've had practice.
haruta_ch6.067: "Hands out of your pockets. It's a whole new silhouette."
haruta_ch6.068: I'm told it suits me. Nobody's given them any blocking yet. I'm open to direction.
haruta_ch6.069: He reaches past you, to the last switch in the corridor. His hand stops over it.
haruta_ch6.070: This one's yours, I think. You used to lock up.
haruta_ch6.071: The corridor goes out. Only the little window is left, violet, NOW and LAST and SHOWING, and the two of you standing in what it can reach.
haruta_ch6.072: On the stairs, he doesn't go first this time, and he doesn't wait. You go down in step, which takes no arranging at all.
haruta_ch6.073: Below, the lobby is filling. There's a line of light along the front desk, and seven voices talking at once, and then, as you arrive, quiet.
haruta_final.001: You say it. *Haruta's.* It comes out fast, before you can dress it.
haruta_final.002: Selection received. RECORD 06. Preparing the card. This takes one minute. I am told a minute is long enough for most things.
haruta_final.003: Halfway up the Archive Wall, one box begins to warm from grey to violet. The others step back a little, the way people do at a door they've decided not to crowd.
haruta_final.004: Haruta is beside you. Hands out of his pockets. He looks at the box, then at you, and he doesn't say thank you yet. He has something else first.
haruta_final.005: I get one follow-up. I've earned exactly one. I counted my tickets.
haruta_final.006: You chose it. I heard. I'm not asking why. {p} I'm asking what tonight was. For you.
haruta_final.007: Fast, if you can. The fast ones are the true ones.
haruta_final.008: "The night I stopped looking for the exit. You were sitting beside it."
haruta_final.009: "The night I found my person. The one I'll always save a seat for."
haruta_final.010: "The first reel of something long. I don't want to hurry the rest."
haruta_ending_beside.001: He takes the sentence in. *My person.* You watch it go all the way down and land somewhere with room for it.
haruta_ending_beside.002: …Yes. {p} That's the word. I've been going round it all night with a torch.
haruta_ending_beside.003: I've been saving you a seat since the lobby. I just thought it was manners.
haruta_ending_beside.004: RECORD 06 — OWNER: HARUTA. PRESERVING. CONTENTS: ONE TICKET STUB, HALF. ONE LINE OF SCRIPT, AMENDED.
haruta_ending_beside.005: One field is empty. RELATION OF SUBJECTS. It used to read "strangers." The owner removed that. I cannot leave a field empty. It itches.
haruta_ending_beside.007: Every small cinema has two people like this. They don't arrive together. They're just always there, the same nights, and the clerk tears two tickets without asking.
haruta_ending_beside.009: Entered: REGULARS. {p} I do not have a definition for this. I find I have several examples.
haruta_ending_beside.010: A thin card of glass slides out of the slot, warm as a cup. The stub. The handwriting. One word struck through, and a new one, very small, in the corner.
haruta_ending_beside.011: Regulars. {p} Yeah. That's you two. You've got the same face when the lights go down.
haruta_ending_beside.012: Do regulars get a discount? I'm asking as someone who has been here since midnight. I feel regular.
haruta_ending_beside.013: You can be a regular too. It isn't a small club. It just has two founding members.
haruta_ending_beside.014: I have ninety seconds. I would like to run the credits. I was promised an audience. It is my only entry under "promises."
haruta_ending_beside.015: The lobby dims into the Dalbit, red seats laid over the old sofas like a double exposure. This time, nobody drifts towards the stairs.
haruta_ending_beside.016: Haruta sits down in the middle of the longest sofa and pats the place on either side. One for you. Then, looking up at the others —
haruta_ending_beside.017: Please sit down. We are about to begin.
haruta_ending_beside.018: They do. All of them. Hyunjun takes the far end. Hanbi takes the arm. Charlie comes last, and room is made for him without anyone having to ask.
haruta_ending_beside.019: HANBI. HAMIN. SONGHA. CHARLIE. HYUNJUN. HARUTA. JUSTIN. DANIEL. {{playerName}}.
haruta_ending_beside.020: SPECIAL THANKS: SEO YEONHWA. MRS OH, GUITAR. THE CAT, WHO DID NOT MOVE.
haruta_ending_beside.021: Nine people watch the names go by to the very end. Your shoulder is against his. It's the easiest thing in the room.
haruta_ending_beside.022: The screen goes white, then grey. Nobody stands up until somebody wants to.
haruta_ending_beside.023: The building is dark, and quiet, and finished. Nine torches find the door.
haruta_ending_beside.024: On the step, he holds your coat open for you, as promised. The outside door, not before. You put your arms in. It's only a coat now.
haruta_ending_beside.025: The corner store. Not the station one. There's a bench outside, under the awning, still beaded with rain.
haruta_ending_beside.026: Inside, through the glass, seven people are failing to form a queue. Hyunjun is reading the order off his hand.
haruta_ending_beside.027: Haruta comes out first, carrying a paper bag against his chest with both arms, like something he isn't going to put down for anyone.
haruta_ending_beside.028: Two egg sandwiches. A strawberry milk. A bag of honey butter chips, unopened, enormous.
haruta_ending_beside.029: And a peach iced tea, cold, which he sets on your side of the bench without comment.
haruta_ending_beside.030: And a hot chocolate, the hot kind, which he sets on your side of the bench without comment.
haruta_ending_beside.031: And a black coffee, no sugar, which he sets on your side of the bench without comment.
haruta_ending_beside.032: And a grape soda, the purple one, which he sets on your side of the bench without comment.
haruta_ending_beside.033: And a second strawberry milk, which he sets on your side of the bench with some ceremony.
haruta_ending_beside.034: I bought a whole bag and I'm not sharing it. {p} Except with you. I've decided that's a different thing from sharing.
haruta_ending_beside.035: He opens it. The first one goes to you. The second one he eats with his eyes shut.
haruta_ending_beside.036: Three years. It's exactly as good as I thought. That almost never happens.
haruta_ending_beside.037: He wipes his fingers carefully on a napkin, and takes the ledger out of his cardigan.
haruta_ending_beside.038: I've been thinking about what a person is. "My person." I want to get it right, because I'm going to be one.
haruta_ending_beside.039: I think it's who you tell first. Before you've made it polite. When I want something, I'd like to say it to you while it's still the wrong shape.
haruta_ending_beside.040: And when I start looking for my coat, I'll tell you. Before I've put it on.
haruta_ending_beside.041: And I won't say "stay." I'll say, "there are hooks." You'll know what I mean.
haruta_ending_beside.042: "I've never had somewhere people expected me back."
haruta_ending_beside.043: You have a mark on a practice-room floor with your name on it. And now a bench. It's a start. I'm going to be very boring about it.
haruta_ending_beside.044: "Regulars get a loyalty card, I assume."
haruta_ending_beside.045: Ten Fridays and the eleventh is also a Friday. It's a very simple scheme.
haruta_ending_beside.046: He opens the ledger on the bench between you. Next Friday's row: his name, your *1*. He writes the date underneath it, the Friday after.
haruta_ending_beside.047: He doesn't fill in CHOSEN BY. He turns the book round and holds out the pencil on its string.
haruta_ending_beside.048: We alternate. Down the whole page. I did the sums. It runs out in about a year and a half, and then I'll buy another book.
haruta_ending_beside.049: You sign. Your name under his. Under that, the columns go on, ruled and empty, and for once an empty row looks like room.
haruta_ending_beside.050: I'm happy. I'm saying it out loud, because I say things now. I'm not going anywhere, and I'm not leaving a seat between us.
haruta_ending_beside.051: The shop door opens. Hyunjun, holding it with one shoulder. Seven people and too many bags.
haruta_ending_beside.052: Haruta shifts along the bench until his arm is against yours, and nods at the space that's left.
haruta_ending_beside.053: Please sit down. I've got an item.
haruta_ending_beside.054: You stay exactly where you are. It turns out you're good at it.
haruta_ending_someday.001: *The first reel.* He says it back without sound, just his mouth. Then he laughs, once, the way you do when someone has read your notes over your shoulder.
haruta_ending_someday.002: That's what I was going to say. Almost to the word. I had "first act."
haruta_ending_someday.003: "Reel" is better. Reels are heavier. You have to carry them up to the booth.
haruta_ending_someday.004: RECORD 06 — OWNER: HARUTA. PRESERVING. CONTENTS: ONE TICKET STUB, HALF. ONE LINE OF SCRIPT, AMENDED.
haruta_ending_someday.005: STATUS OF SCENE: UNFINISHED. {p} Earlier tonight I would have marked that as an error. I have removed the error. "Unfinished" is now a status.
haruta_ending_someday.006: A thin card of glass slides out of the slot, warm as a cup. The stub, the handwriting, the one word struck through. It fits his palm exactly.
haruta_ending_someday.007: Unfinished. Do you want me to put a date on it? I have a calendar. I have four calendars.
haruta_ending_someday.008: Not yet. I'll tell you when there's a date. {p} There's going to be a date.
haruta_ending_someday.009: He said it like a man booking a venue. I'm leaving a line free.
haruta_ending_someday.011: Hanbi hands over a paper sleeve, the right size for a card. Of course he has one.
haruta_ending_someday.012: I have ninety seconds. I was promised an audience for the credits. It is my only entry under "promises." I would like it kept.
haruta_ending_someday.013: The lobby dims into the Dalbit one more time. The others take the back rows, noisily, then quietly. Row F is left alone, the way you leave a table for two people still talking.
haruta_ending_someday.014: HANBI. HAMIN. SONGHA. CHARLIE. HYUNJUN. HARUTA. JUSTIN. DANIEL. {{playerName}}.
haruta_ending_someday.015: SPECIAL THANKS: SEO YEONHWA. THE CAT. {p} TO BE CONTINUED — that last line is not standard. I added it. Nobody has objected.
haruta_ending_someday.016: Seat seven and seat eight. His sleeve on the armrest next to yours. You stay until the screen goes grey, and a moment after.
haruta_ending_someday.017: Dark, and quiet, and the door that was never locked.
haruta_ending_someday.018: On the step, he holds your coat open for you. The outside door, as promised. You put your arms in. It's only a coat now.
haruta_ending_someday.019: The others have gone ahead to the corner store. He asked them to. Out loud, in front of everyone: *we'll catch up — I want ten minutes.* Nobody made a joke. Daniel nodded once, like a man witnessing a signature.
haruta_ending_someday.020: He walks you two streets over instead, to a shuttered key-cutting shop with a narrow staircase beside it. A dark sign. A schedule taped inside the glass.
haruta_ending_someday.021: The Dalbit. The real one. It's been eight minutes away all night.
haruta_ending_someday.022: He stands in front of it with his hands at his sides. Not in his pockets. You know what that means now.
haruta_ending_someday.023: I'm going to say something, and then I'm going to say a second thing. Please wait for the second one. They go together.
haruta_ending_someday.024: I like you. {p} Not the way I like a regular, or a good seat. I like you the way I wanted honey butter. For a long time, specifically, and I kept saying something else.
haruta_ending_someday.025: That's the first thing. It's true. I checked it on a roof.
haruta_ending_someday.027: …Specifically. {p} All right. I needed a second. I've had it.
haruta_ending_someday.028: Take your hand out of your own pocket, and hold it out. Let him see it's the same answer.
haruta_ending_someday.029: He looks at it. He puts his hand in yours, briefly, completely, like signing something. Then he gives it back so he can finish.
haruta_ending_someday.030: I thought so. I hoped so. I'd like to hear it as well, some time. Not now. I'm mid-speech.
haruta_ending_someday.033: Here's the second thing. I learned to want things about four hours ago. I'm still new at it. Tonight I ordered an egg sandwich, and my hands weren't steady.
haruta_ending_someday.034: I don't want you to be what I practise on. I want to be good at it by the time it's you.
haruta_ending_someday.035: It isn't an apology. He says it like a director asking for one more week before the opening, because the film deserves it.
haruta_ending_someday.036: I have a second thing too.
haruta_ending_someday.037: I've never stayed anywhere past spring. I want to find out that I can. For myself, first. Before I promise it to somebody I like this much.
haruta_ending_someday.038: Then we're asking for the same thing. We just came at it from opposite aisles.
haruta_ending_someday.039: Not "no." Not "later, maybe." A date. With a date on it.
haruta_ending_someday.040: He turns to the schedule in the glass and runs his finger down the column, reading slowly, as he did three years ago. He reads it easily now.
haruta_ending_someday.041: The first Friday of March. The late screening. Ten past eleven. Row F.
haruta_ending_someday.042: You always left in spring. I'd like to be standing here when it arrives, and see you coming up the street.
haruta_ending_someday.043: "First Friday of March. I'll be here."
haruta_ending_someday.044: I know. That's the strange part. I'm not even nervous about it. I'm only nervous about what to wear.
haruta_ending_someday.046: I do. It'll be terrible. You bring the cushion.
haruta_ending_someday.047: They have seats, I know. Bring it anyway. It's the principle.
haruta_ending_someday.049: Every Friday. Film club. I'll sit next to you, and I won't pretend I've forgotten this, and neither will you.
haruta_ending_someday.050: We'll just let it come at its own speed. Like credits. You can't make them go faster. I've tried.
haruta_ending_someday.051: He takes out his half of the lavender flyer. You find yours, in the pocket where it has been all night. FRIDAY FILM on one. CLUB. BRING A CUSHION on the other.
haruta_ending_someday.052: He turns yours over and writes on the back with the ledger's pencil, leaning on the Dalbit's door. The date. 23:10. *Row F.*
haruta_ending_someday.053: Then he holds out his own half, blank side up, and the pencil.
haruta_ending_someday.054: You write mine. So we each have it in the other one's handwriting. Neither of us can say we misread.
haruta_ending_someday.055: You write it. The date. The time. After a moment, underneath: *I'm not going anywhere. Take your time.*
haruta_ending_someday.056: That's my favourite line. {p} You knew that.
haruta_ending_someday.057: He holds his half up. You hold up yours. The torn edges meet, not straight, the way a ticket is torn at the door, and for a second it is one flyer again.
haruta_ending_someday.058: Then you each take back your own. The smaller half. The part they give you to keep.
haruta_ending_someday.059: Breakfast? I've got an item at ten past six, and a whole bag of something I'm not sharing.
haruta_ending_someday.060: Except with you. In March, and also now.
haruta_ending_someday.061: The sun comes up on a shuttered cinema with a schedule taped inside its window. You walk to the corner store side by side.
haruta_ending_someday.062: Neither of you hurries. It's a long film, and you've only seen the first reel.
justin_ch1.001: Every route through this building passes the front desk. That was the whole idea of the front desk.
justin_ch1.002: Justin has walked past it all night. This time he stops, and puts both elbows on the counter, and leans over to look at the side customers never see.
justin_ch1.004: Smaller than it looks. There's a heater under the desk that only warms your left foot.
justin_ch1.006: The right one learns to cope.
justin_ch1.007: The counter flap sticks. It always did. You lift, then push, and it swings up the way it swung up a hundred nights one winter.
justin_ch1.008: Your hands knew how before you'd decided to try.
justin_ch1.009: You didn't even look at it. I know what that is. That's a routine.
justin_ch1.010: Is there a book? There was a book. I had to write my name in a book.
justin_ch1.011: Second drawer from the bottom. It needs a hip, not a hand. You give it the hip.
justin_ch1.012: Inside: a stapler, a dead torch, a ring of keys with a cracked plastic 25 on the tag — and a green hardback ledger, soft at the corners.
justin_ch1.013: ROOM HIRE, it says on the cover, in marker. Underneath, in a different marker: *please write clearly. please.*
justin_ch1.014: That's it. That's the book. I'm in there somewhere.
justin_ch1.015: February. Three years ago. I want to see what I wrote. I was so nervous I think I spelled my own name wrong.
justin_ch1.016: "Easy. We look for the worst handwriting."
justin_ch1.017: Rude. Accurate. My sevens look like ones and my ones look like accidents.
justin_ch1.018: He flips pages fast, the way he does everything, and overshoots February twice.
justin_ch1.019: "Tell me the date. I'll find the night."
justin_ch1.020: The ninth. No — the tenth, technically. It was after midnight.
justin_ch1.021: You turn the pages for him. Slowly. He watches your hands instead of the book.
justin_ch1.022: Turn straight to the page with the coffee ring.
justin_ch1.023: February had a coffee ring on it. You put it there. You remember being annoyed at yourself for a week.
justin_ch1.024: You knew exactly where that was.
justin_ch1.025: I spilled on it. I felt terrible. It's a very easy month to find.
justin_ch1.026: And there it is. One line among a lot of lines.
justin_ch1.027: ROOM B. IN: 00:30. NAME: a J, and then a small, panicked scribble.
justin_ch1.028: PURPOSE: *dance*, crossed out. *practice*, crossed out. And then, pressed hard enough to dent the paper: *nothing*.
justin_ch1.030: I remember that. I didn't want anybody to read "dance" and come and look.
justin_ch1.031: Great plan. Flawless. Nobody came to look. Except the one person with the keys.
justin_ch1.032: He runs a finger along the line to the next column, and stops.
justin_ch1.033: OUT: 01:00. It isn't his handwriting. It's rounder. It leans the other way.
justin_ch1.035: One o'clock. But I wasn't out at one. You stood in the door at — what, ten to? And then I did the bad eight, and then I packed up *so* slowly—
justin_ch1.036: It was twenty past. At least. I looked at the clock in the lobby and felt sick.
justin_ch1.037: There's a laminated card still taped to the desk. LATE FINISH: 1,500 WON PER TEN MINUTES. Someone has drawn a small sad face next to the number.
justin_ch1.038: So I've owed this building three thousand won for three years. That's not a record I wanted.
justin_ch1.039: He's already reaching into his hoodie pocket. He comes up with a folded five-thousand note and looks around for somewhere official to put it.
justin_ch1.040: The honesty tin is where it always was, behind the stapler. It rattles with exactly one coin.
justin_ch1.041: "I wrote one o'clock on purpose. You looked like you needed the twenty minutes."
justin_ch1.042: He stops with the note halfway to the tin.
justin_ch1.044: They weren't mine to charge for. Nobody else wanted the room.
justin_ch1.045: I thought I got away with it. I didn't get away with anything. Somebody just let me.
justin_ch1.046: "With three years of interest, that's one strawberry milk. Exactly."
justin_ch1.047: One strawberry milk. I can't pay that. I have a complicated history with strawberry milk.
justin_ch1.049: Everyone's heard. Hyunjun makes sure of it.
justin_ch1.050: Put the lid back on the tin. "Desk's closed."
justin_ch1.051: He looks at the tin. At the note. At you.

songha_ending_beside.023: At 05:40 he walked everyone to the station, exactly as written. He counted seven heads through the barrier and said "text when you're home" seven times.
songha_ending_beside.024: Then he turned round instead of going through. You had already turned round.
songha_ending_beside.025: The foreman with the hard hat gave you the roof until half past six, in exchange for nothing. People are kind at that hour.
songha_ending_beside.026: So it's the chair that doesn't wobble and the crate, and two warm cans from the shop by the station, and a sky going the colour of peach skin at one edge.
songha_ending_beside.027: 06:14. Sunrise. It's on time. I take no credit.
songha_ending_beside.028: He has the notebook open to TOMORROW. The line that's been empty since four o'clock. *07:00 —*
songha_ending_beside.029: I know what goes there now.
songha_ending_beside.030: He writes it and turns the page toward you, a quarter-inch, the way he did at midnight. *07:00 — breakfast. (You pick.)*
songha_ending_beside.031: Okay. The word. I said I'd say it up here.
songha_ending_beside.032: I've got seven people I'd do anything for. I know their shoe sizes. I know who's lying about having slept.
songha_ending_beside.033: What I've never had is someone I hand the list to. I didn't know it was missing. You don't, until somebody holds it for ten minutes and nothing falls down.
songha_ending_beside.034: You're my person. That's the word. I looked for a better one on the stairs. There isn't one.
songha_ending_beside.035: You're mine. I've never stayed anywhere long enough to have one. I'd like to start with you.
songha_ending_beside.036: He nods, once, like a thing confirmed. Then the nod gives up and turns into the whole smile.
songha_ending_beside.037: It's not a smaller thing. I want that said plainly. It's the thing I didn't have.
songha_ending_beside.038: So. When you were sixteen, you told me you didn't know what you were doing on Thursday.
songha_ending_beside.040: You do now. Thursdays. You and me. Anywhere with a table.
songha_ending_beside.041: It's not a plan. It's a standing item. Standing items don't get ticked. They just keep happening.
songha_ending_beside.043: You tell me what went wrong that week. I give you three things I'd do about it. You ignore two.
songha_ending_beside.044: Then you take the notebook for an hour, and I sit down. Actually sit.
songha_ending_beside.045: And when it's 5:40 and it's heavy?
songha_ending_beside.046: Then I text you. That's the rule. I've never had that rule. {p} I like it already.
songha_ending_beside.047: And when you feel like setting the alarm—
songha_ending_beside.049: Before. Not after, from another city. Before. I'll answer. I'm up at 5:40. I'm famously available.
songha_ending_beside.050: You laugh. He laughs, the loud one, and doesn't cover his mouth. A pigeon leaves the water tank in protest.
songha_ending_beside.051: The sun clears the rooftops. Below, the renovation crew are carrying the first things out of Studio 25: a sofa cushion, a lamp, the rubber plant.
songha_ending_beside.052: My letter asked whether I'd found a place I want to stay.
songha_ending_beside.054: I don't think it's a place. I think it's a Thursday.
songha_ending_beside.055: I'm going to write that down. Not the time. Just the sentence.
songha_ending_beside.056: You take out your phone. You open the clock, and you do something you have never done in any city. You set an alarm for arriving.
songha_ending_beside.058: He reads it upside down. He reads everything upside down. He doesn't say a word about it, which from him is an entire speech.
songha_ending_beside.059: His watch is still ticking in the pocket of the jacket you're still wearing. He hasn't asked for either.
songha_ending_beside.062: The building behind you is emptying. The morning isn't. You stay on the good chair and the crate until the cans are finished.
songha_ending_beside.063: Two names at the top of a rota, and nothing at all written under *07:00* but breakfast.
songha_ending_someday.001: He takes that in. You watch him not ask what it is. You watch him want to, very much, and set it down.
songha_ending_someday.002: Then don't say it in forty seconds.
songha_ending_someday.003: I'd rather have it properly. I can wait. I've recently learned how. There's a record of it.
songha_ending_someday.004: On the Wall, every box goes dark but one.
songha_ending_someday.005: Record 03 selected. Owner: Songha. Writing to glass.
songha_ending_someday.006: Contents: one page. Five items. Year Five: open.
songha_ending_someday.007: Appended: one first draft. One word amended by the owner tonight, from "replace" to "keep".
songha_ending_someday.008: Appended: one item, not yet said. I have left room for it on the glass. I am learning to leave room.
songha_ending_someday.009: The card slides out, warm and faintly lit. In one corner there is a small clear space with nothing engraved in it. It catches the light differently from the rest.
songha_ending_someday.010: There's a blank bit. ECHO left him a blank bit. Hyung, you've infected the building.
songha_ending_someday.014: Understood. {p} Still not a no, though.
songha_ending_someday.015: It's the hold, hyung. You're on eight. Don't rush it.
songha_ending_someday.016: A scene that ends just before the line. I like those. The line plays over the next scene.
songha_ending_someday.017: Hanbi says nothing. He looks at the clear corner of the glass, and then at the two of you, and he puts his pen back in his coat without ever having taken the cap off.
songha_ending_someday.018: Songha holds the card out for you to carry. His thumb covers the blank corner until the last moment, as though it could get cold.
songha_ending_someday.019: The stairwell was dark, so he went first with the phone torch and said "step" at every step. There were forty-one. He didn't count them aloud. You heard him counting anyway.
songha_ending_someday.020: The roof at 05:40 is grey and soft, and smells of rain drying. The good chair. The crate. One last star, low in the south.
songha_ending_someday.021: He stands with his hands in his hoodie pocket and doesn't prompt you. It may be the hardest thing he has done tonight, and tonight he tore a page out of his own notebook.
songha_ending_someday.023: I like you. Not the list, and not the jacket. You. The person who asks first, every time.
songha_ending_someday.024: He doesn't answer at once. He doesn't reach for the pen either.
songha_ending_someday.025: Give me a second. Not to plan. Just to have heard it.
songha_ending_someday.026: You give him the second. He takes three.
songha_ending_someday.027: I like you too. {p} There. No steps.
songha_ending_someday.028: I liked you at seventeen for calling a star Gerald. I liked you again from about half past midnight. Those are two separate likings, and I've got both of them.
songha_ending_someday.030: He stops. He shuts his eyes for a moment, and laughs under his breath.
songha_ending_someday.031: I was about to schedule it. I had a first step ready. It was a good first step.
songha_ending_someday.033: I'm not telling you. It'll keep.
songha_ending_someday.034: He sits down on the crate. You take the chair. The sky does the slow thing skies do.
songha_ending_someday.035: Here's the honest part. This is the year on the page. The next few months are going to take everything I've got, and I want to give them that.
songha_ending_someday.036: I don't want to give you whatever's left over at eleven at night. I've seen what's left over. It's a man reading a rota.
songha_ending_someday.037: Here's mine. I've only just stopped setting alarms for leaving. About an hour ago.
songha_ending_someday.038: I'd like to learn to stay somewhere before I ask someone to be the reason.
songha_ending_someday.039: He listens to the whole of it. He doesn't offer a single suggestion. You can see him not doing it.
songha_ending_someday.041: It's the opposite of a no. It's "hold. He'll ask."
songha_ending_someday.042: You're quoting the ledger at me.
songha_ending_someday.043: It's a good ledger. It works. It just runs slow.
songha_ending_someday.044: Then it arrives when it arrives. Both of us decide that. Not me on my own with a pen. {p} I want that on the record.
songha_ending_someday.046: Then you'll have to remember it the hard way. So will I.
songha_ending_someday.047: He looks east, low down, where the rooftops meet the sky. There is nothing there yet.
songha_ending_someday.048: ECHO said Gerald comes back every winter. Before dawn. Nobody schedules it.
songha_ending_someday.049: The first clear morning he's back. That's when.
songha_ending_someday.050: I'm going to try not to look up the date. I give myself a week.
songha_ending_someday.052: Haneul Park. The top of the stairs. It faces east, and there's nothing in the way.
songha_ending_someday.053: Two hundred and ninety-one steps. I've counted. Obviously I've counted.
songha_ending_someday.055: 5:40. I'll be awake anyway. That morning it gets to be for something else.
songha_ending_someday.057: The watch. Keep it till then. You can give it back up there. Or not. We'll know.
songha_ending_someday.058: I'll bring the draft, and the pen. And two cans. I know which.
songha_ending_someday.060: I'm not writing the line after that. I'm leaving it open on purpose. Second time in my life. It's getting easier.
songha_ending_someday.061: He holds out his hand. Not to shake on it. Palm up, open, the way you would offer to take something heavy from someone.
songha_ending_someday.062: I don't shake on things without dates. This is just my hand. {p} If you'd like it.
songha_ending_someday.063: You take it. It's warm. He holds on for a count of eight, and you both know where the hold is.
songha_ending_someday.064: The last star goes out in the south. The east stays empty, a clean strip of sky above the laundromat, with plenty of room in it.
songha_ending_someday.065: Somewhere below that line, on nobody's schedule, a faint orange star is already on its way.
songha_ending_someday.066: You know its real name now. You'll call it Gerald when it gets here. He'll let you.
hanbi_ch1.001: His hand is still held out. You haven't decided what to do about it yet when the ceiling clears its throat.
hanbi_ch1.003: I announced 04:57. It is 03:10. I apologise.
hanbi_ch1.004: Time spent inside a reconstruction is not charged to the night. I counted it anyway. I was built to be early.
hanbi_ch1.005: Please disregard the summons. You have one hour and forty-seven minutes.
hanbi_ch1.007: He looks at his hand as if it belongs to someone who was very sure of himself a minute ago.
hanbi_ch1.008: Take it, stand up, and sit straight back down. "False alarm."
hanbi_ch1.009: He gets pulled down with you. The sofa makes a noise like an accordion being apologised to.
hanbi_ch1.011: "Good. I wasn't ready to go yet."
hanbi_ch1.013: I'd only just started saying things. I'd like to keep going.
hanbi_ch1.014: Stay where you are. Let the extra hour arrive.
hanbi_ch1.015: He lowers his hand slowly and sits back down beside you. Neither of you mentions it. It was a good hand. It'll keep.
hanbi_ch1.017: What do you usually do with extra time?
hanbi_ch1.018: …I don't know. I've never had any. I give it to whoever's running late.
hanbi_ch1.019: He looks around the lounge for something that needs doing. His eyes stop at the low table by the window, where the dust sheet sits oddly over a flat shape.
hanbi_ch1.020: He lifts a corner the way you'd lift a blanket off a sleeping cat.
hanbi_ch1.021: A jigsaw. A thousand pieces, a harbour at dusk, almost finished. There's a gap in the sky the size of two open hands.
hanbi_ch1.022: The box lid is propped behind it. Taped to the lid, in marker gone brown with age: *DO NOT PUT AWAY. NEARLY DONE.*
hanbi_ch1.023: …It was here. That winter. I remember people doing two pieces on their way to the door.
hanbi_ch1.025: …Nobody put it away. They just covered it.
hanbi_ch1.026: …Someone should finish it. Before the morning. It shouldn't go in a skip with a hole in it.
hanbi_ch1.027: We have an hour and forty-seven minutes.
hanbi_ch1.029: The loose pieces are in the lid. Forty or so, and every one of them is sky.
hanbi_ch1.030: "How do you tell them apart? They're all the same blue."
hanbi_ch1.032: He lays three in a row on his palm. You look. They're the same blue.
hanbi_ch1.033: That one's tired. That one's got the sun behind it. That one's nearly a cloud.
hanbi_ch1.034: You look again. Annoyingly, he's right.
hanbi_ch1.035: "I'll take the tired blues. You take the smug ones."
hanbi_ch1.037: The ones near the sunset. They know what they've got.
hanbi_ch1.038: He sorts them into two piles without another word. He gives you the easier pile and thinks you haven't noticed.
hanbi_ch1.041: They always went back in the box when we moved. Four cities. Four boxes of nearly.
hanbi_ch1.042: …Then it's two people's first. That's better. Neither of us knows how it's supposed to feel.
hanbi_ch1.043: You work. It's slow and it's easy. The lamp hums. His sleeve brushes yours when he reaches for the top corner. The first time, he glances over to check. After that he leaves his chair where it is, and so do you.
hanbi_ch1.044: He talks more than you expected. It's all colours.
hanbi_ch1.045: Not that one. That's— grey-blue. Rain colour. It goes lower.
hanbi_ch1.046: …This is the last of the orange. Where the sun was.
hanbi_ch1.047: You realise what he's doing a few pieces later. He's saying them out loud. Nobody asked him to.
hanbi_ch1.049: …Practice. Tell me if you'd rather I stopped.
hanbi_ch1.051: The gap closes from the edges in. Two open hands. One. A fist. A thumbprint.
hanbi_ch1.052: Then the lid is empty, and there is one hole left in the sky.
hanbi_ch1.054: Tell me there's one in your sleeve.
hanbi_ch1.055: There isn't. There isn't one under the table or inside the box, either. You both check twice.
hanbi_ch1.056: You go down on your knees and feel under the orange sofa. You come up with a guitar pick, a hundred-won coin, and a great deal of dust.
hanbi_ch1.057: Guitar pick. From the man who was asleep on his case, probably.
hanbi_ch1.058: …Keep the coin. It's been waiting longest.
hanbi_ch1.059: You put the coin in your coat pocket. He looks at the hole in the sky the way he looks at a page.
hanbi_ch1.060: Then he opens his sketchbook at the back, where the cover is stiff grey card, and lays it against the puzzle.
hanbi_ch1.061: He traces the hole. Four quick curves. He scores the line with his thumbnail and works the shape out of the card with slow, patient folds.
hanbi_ch1.062: A jigsaw piece. Grey, and a little furry at the edges, and the right size.
hanbi_ch1.063: …What colour was it? The sky. There.
hanbi_ch1.065: …Neither have I. Somebody has to say.
hanbi_ch1.066: He's already holding the tin open. The yellow pencil is the shortest one in it, by now. Laundromat yellow.
hanbi_ch1.067: A lit window. Somebody left a light on, over the water.
hanbi_ch1.069: He's already holding the tin open. The green pencil is the shortest one in it, by now. Exit-sign green.
hanbi_ch1.070: Green. One of those strange skies you get right after the sun goes.
hanbi_ch1.072: He's already holding the tin open. The red pencil is the shortest one in it, by now. Vending-machine red.
hanbi_ch1.073: Red. The very last of the sunset. One dot of it.
hanbi_ch1.075: He's already holding the tin open. The blue pencil is the shortest one in it, by now. Archive Wall blue.
hanbi_ch1.076: Blue. A bit brighter than the rest. Like something's glowing behind it.
hanbi_ch1.078: He colours the card in small even strokes and holds it out to you, flat on his palm.
hanbi_ch1.080: Put two fingers on one edge of the piece. Wait for his. "Together."
hanbi_ch1.081: He looks at your fingers. Then he puts his own on the other edge, and you carry it over the harbour like something that could spill.
hanbi_ch1.082: It goes in with the small soft click that cardboard makes. Neither of you takes your hand away first.
hanbi_ch1.083: Try it upside down first. Frown. Turn it. Try again.
hanbi_ch1.085: I'm building suspense. Six years. It deserves a moment.
hanbi_ch1.086: It goes in. He tips his head to you, once, the way you'd acknowledge a good shot across a quiet room.
hanbi_ch1.087: "No. You. You never get to finish things."
hanbi_ch1.088: He holds the piece over the gap for a long time. His hand is steady. He isn't hesitating. He's taking his time over it.
hanbi_ch1.089: Then he presses it in with one finger, and lets out a breath like someone putting down shopping.
hanbi_ch1.090: A harbour at dusk. Finished. One piece of the sky is the wrong colour, and it's the only part you can look at.
hanbi_ch1.091: …It's strange. I thought it would feel worse.
hanbi_ch1.093: …I like things when they're almost done. You noticed.
hanbi_ch1.094: When something's finished, people say "that's nice," and put it away. It goes in a box. It goes on a shelf.
hanbi_ch1.095: If it's nearly done, it has to stay out. People have to keep coming back to it.
hanbi_ch1.096: He touches the old note on the lid. *DO NOT PUT AWAY.*
hanbi_ch1.097: …I think I've been this note. About a lot of things.
hanbi_ch1.098: The portrait. I told you I wasn't ready to decide. That's true.
hanbi_ch1.099: But I was also scared. That if I finished your face, tonight would be finished. And you'd go back in the box.
hanbi_ch1.100: He says it plainly, to the puzzle, and then makes himself look up and say the last part to you.
hanbi_ch1.101: …I was afraid of that. I'd rather you knew.
hanbi_ch1.102: "Then we leave it out. Finished, and out. Both."
hanbi_ch1.104: I've packed a lot of boxes. I know what I put in them, and it was never the things I'd finished. It was the things I'd given up on.
hanbi_ch1.106: "I'm much too awkward a shape for a box."
hanbi_ch1.107: …You are. I've been trying to draw it all night.
hanbi_ch1.109: Turn the lid over and hold the marker out to him.
hanbi_ch1.110: There's a marker in the box, dried almost to nothing. You hold it out. He understands at once. He usually does.
hanbi_ch1.111: He takes the pencil from behind his ear and writes on the lid, under the old note, in small careful capitals.
hanbi_ch1.113: …There. Now it's somebody else's problem. In a good way.
hanbi_ch2.001: The lobby is louder than you left it. The noise is coming from the claw machine.
hanbi_ch2.002: It had the bear by the ear. You saw that. Then it let go, and I'd say it was deliberate.
hanbi_ch2.003: It didn't let go. It *released* it. There's a difference, and the bear knows it.
hanbi_ch2.004: Hyunjun is sitting on the floor among the convenience-store bags, sorting what's left into eight fair piles.
hanbi_ch2.005: Hanbi takes his corner of the sofa. The sketchbook comes out. Hyunjun notices at once.
hanbi_ch2.006: Hyung. Draw me. You drew Daniel's face when the building talked. I saw it over your shoulder, and it was good. I'd like one.
hanbi_ch2.007: You drew my face when, exactly?
hanbi_ch2.011: …Any longer and I start being kind. Then it doesn't look like anyone.
hanbi_ch2.012: I'll time it. I'm a fair timekeeper. Go.
hanbi_ch2.013: Thirty seconds of Hanbi drawing is a different thing from an afternoon of it. No apologising. The pencil doesn't leave the page once.
hanbi_ch2.015: Hyunjun: a great deal of hair, an easy grin, and a triangle kimbap in one hand, half unwrapped.
hanbi_ch2.016: That's me. No argument. How did the kimbap get in? I wasn't holding one.
hanbi_ch2.018: Daniel gets a level, stubborn brow and, in the corner, a tiny claw with a bear held firmly by one ear.
hanbi_ch2.021: Daniel looks at the page for a moment without saying anything. Then he nods, once, and sets it down with care.
hanbi_ch2.022: All right. New round. {{playerName}} draws hyung.
hanbi_ch2.024: Seconded. Thirty seconds, same rule. It's only fair.
hanbi_ch2.025: Hanbi goes still. He isn't reluctant. It's more that nobody has ever pointed that question at him before.
hanbi_ch2.026: Then he turns the sketchbook round on his knee and holds out the pencil, the one from behind his ear.
hanbi_ch2.027: …You don't have to be good. I told you. I'd just like to see it.
hanbi_ch2.029: Start with the pencil behind the ear. Get the important things down first.
hanbi_ch2.030: You draw the pencil. It comes out well. It's a very good pencil. After that there are twenty-four seconds left and an entire person to fit round it.
hanbi_ch2.031: Start with the eyes. The way they look at a page.
hanbi_ch2.032: You look up to check. He's looking straight back, holding still the way he asked you to hold still. It costs you four seconds you don't have.
hanbi_ch2.033: Start with the hair. Ask for the blue pencil.
hanbi_ch2.034: He passes the tin without a word. You scribble a sea on top of where a head will shortly need to be. It's bold. You can't undo it now.
hanbi_ch2.035: Thirty seconds turns out to be no time at all. You draw faster. It gets worse. You add a cardigan, because a cardigan is mostly rectangles.
hanbi_ch2.036: Time. Pencils down. Show the court.
hanbi_ch2.038: Nobody says anything for a moment.
hanbi_ch2.039: It's a potato. There's no way round it. A gentle, slightly lopsided potato in a cardigan, with a pencil behind where an ear would go.
hanbi_ch2.040: It's smiling, though. You got that part. It has exactly his small closed smile.
hanbi_ch2.041: I like him. He looks like someone you'd trust with your keys.
hanbi_ch2.042: That's him. I mean it. That's what he's like to be around. Frame it.
hanbi_ch2.043: You risk a look at the subject.
hanbi_ch2.044: Hanbi is laughing the way he does. No sound at all, shoulders going, one hand flat over his eyes.
hanbi_ch2.045: When the hand comes down, he isn't laughing any more. He's looking at the potato quite seriously.
hanbi_ch2.049: Nobody's drawn me before. I'm always the one holding the pencil.
hanbi_ch2.050: "Then it's yours. I'll do a better one when I've had more than thirty seconds."
hanbi_ch2.051: …Don't make it better. Make another one. They're different things.
hanbi_ch2.052: Sign it. Large. With a flourish.
hanbi_ch2.053: You sign it across the bottom corner like a bank manager. He watches every stroke of your name.
hanbi_ch2.055: Turn the book back round to him, and leave your hand on the page a second longer.
hanbi_ch2.056: He takes the book back carefully, his fingers beside yours on the paper, as if the potato might smudge.
hanbi_ch2.057: Trade you, hyung. For the portrait.
hanbi_ch2.058: Hyunjun sets a banana milk on the armrest. Then he sets a second one next to it, for you, as if that went without saying.
hanbi_ch2.059: I'm going back in. The bear and I have unfinished business.
hanbi_ch2.060: I'll spot you one more coin. After that you're negotiating with the machine on your own.
hanbi_ch2.061: They go. The claw machine starts its awful little song again. Hanbi hasn't turned the page.
hanbi_ch2.062: He's gone back to the lobby drawing from the start of the night. The front desk. The Archive Wall, box by box. The sofas.
hanbi_ch2.063: You look at it properly, for the first time since he finished it.
hanbi_ch2.064: Everyone's in it. Songha with his phone up. Charlie mid-question. Justin stealing something out of Hyunjun's bag. Hamin counting heads.
hanbi_ch2.065: And on the end of the far sofa, a row of water bottles on an armrest, and nobody beside them.
hanbi_ch2.069: He looks at the page. It takes him a second to understand the question, and that second tells you more than the answer does.
hanbi_ch2.071: You were also the one sitting there.
hanbi_ch2.072: …I don't usually. Put myself in. It's— the page is for who I'm looking at.
hanbi_ch2.073: He tries to say it like a rule of the craft. It comes out sounding like something smaller and older.
hanbi_ch2.074: …I think I forget. That I'm in the room.
hanbi_ch2.075: "Somebody was sitting there. I saw him. He gave me his water."
hanbi_ch2.077: You remember where I was sitting.
hanbi_ch2.078: Far end. So you could see everyone. It was the first thing I noticed about you.
hanbi_ch2.079: He puts the pencil to the empty cushion. It takes him thirty seconds. He doesn't make it kind.
hanbi_ch2.080: A tall shape, a bit rounded at the shoulders, with a sketchbook on its knee. It's the first drawing of himself you've seen.
hanbi_ch2.081: "May I?" Take the pencil, and put the potato in the empty seat.
hanbi_ch2.082: You draw it small, in the corner of the sofa. A potato in a cardigan, a pencil behind its ear, presiding over seven bottles of water.
hanbi_ch2.083: …That's going to be in there forever.
hanbi_ch2.084: Good. He was there. He should be on the record.
hanbi_ch2.086: Hold out your hand for the pencil. Let him choose who holds it.
hanbi_ch2.087: He looks at your open hand. Then he keeps the pencil, and nods, and bends over the page himself.
hanbi_ch2.088: Nine quick lines. A tall shape with a sketchbook on its knee. He leaves the face for last, from habit. Then he does the face.
hanbi_ch2.089: The lobby drawing has nine people in it now.
hanbi_ch2.090: He holds the book out at arm's length and looks at it the way you look at a photograph that you turn out to be in.
hanbi_ch2.093: …You keep doing that to my things tonight.
hanbi_ch2.094: He opens the banana milk Hyunjun left, and hands you yours with the straw already in. Then he drinks his own. All of it, not the polite half.
hanbi_ch2.095: …Thirty seconds is a long time. When you're the one being looked at.
hanbi_ch2.096: You've been doing it to me all night.
hanbi_ch2.098: A pause. You watch him go back for the sentence.
hanbi_ch2.099: …No. I'm not sorry. I'd do it again. I'm sorry I didn't ask first.
hanbi_ch2.104: Across the lobby the claw machine plays its losing tune. Daniel's voice says, with great dignity, "One more."

daniel_ending_someday.043: Four thousand won. You still owe me for the first one.
daniel_ending_someday.045: I'll waive the interest. I'm not waiving the four thousand. It's the principle.
daniel_ending_someday.046: You take the pen out of your coat. It's still Songha's. You write it on the back of your half, under his arrow, where *FRAME NINE →* points off the edge of the paper.
daniel_ending_someday.048: He reads it over your arm, and then holds out his own half for you to write it there too, so that both copies say the same thing.
daniel_ending_someday.049: On the folded page there's a twelve with two small words after it, in his writing: *a next one*. He takes the pen and, carefully, adds a date.
daniel_ending_someday.050: Then the sun comes up. It just does it. Over the laundromat, with no help from anyone, one bright edge and then all of it.
daniel_ending_someday.052: He gets the list out. He doesn't tick it. He gives you the page, and holds the pen with you, and the two of you make one slightly crooked tick together.
daniel_ending_someday.053: Done. Everything's closed. Songha's going to frame it.
daniel_ending_someday.054: I can hear you. I'm on the stairs. Breakfast is in nine minutes and I'm two people short.
daniel_ending_someday.057: Four minutes. You spend them doing nothing, side by side at a low wall, with the light coming across the roof and warming one half of each of you.
daniel_ending_someday.058: You're not leaving, and nothing is ending. There's a night in July with your name on it, and a week before that with a booth in it, and breakfast in four minutes.
daniel_ending_someday.059: For the first time you can remember, there's somewhere you have to be later. Daniel hums. It sounds a little like rain.
